messages.author: 31159c9ecd804c46
messages.subject: Survey design problem
parts:
Dear Distance Users/Developers:

I am in the process of designing a helicopter survey for
kangaroos. I have done this before. In this instance, I have six
zones that I want to survey; each of which is subdivided into two or
three strata. My strategy for designing these surveys is to use the
automated survey design engine in DISTANCE 6.0 to design a survey
separately for each stratum using the systematic segmented trackline
and the systematic segmented grid design options. The general design
includes "Minus sampling" and "Keeping complete samplers". To decide
on the final design, I compare the coverages of the two design
options across 999 simulations.

I have run into an execution problem (see below) with the systematic
segmented grid design (10 km samplers) on one of the strata (3,185
sq. km in area) in one of my zones (in which two of the three strata
are to be surveyed). The development of a systematic segmented
trackline design was successful for this stratum. The development of
both design options was successfully completed for the other stratum
( 2,300 sq. km in area) to be surveyed in this zone.

The information below is the contents of the output log. It may not
be enough information for anyone to offer a definitive
comment. However, if anyone can see from this what I might be doing
wrong (no matter how dopey it is), I would appreciate the feedback.

Regards,
Stuart

Mandy (and Stuart):

I don't remember if we resolved this problem back in 2012, but the error message cryptically notes Distance is seeking a field name that it cannot locate.  I deduce this from the error being generated by a function "....ValidFieldName"  I don't know what field it cannot locate, but if you Export your project "File | Export" from the main menu, I can have a look and see if I can resolve this.

messages.author: 8e77e57d5ced030f
messages.subject: Re: Survey design problem
parts:
Hello Eric and Stuart,

I appreciate your quick response. I think I figured out what the problem was in my case, and I'm embarrassed that it was such a simple fix. The coverage layer I was attempting to use became corrupted, and therefore I was unable to calculate coverage probabilities. I'm sorry your issue has not been resolved, Stuart. I wish you luck in your field work!

Thank you both for your time and consideration. I am just starting to use DISTANCE, so it's comforting to know there is such a strong support group. I am grateful for all you do!

Best,

Mandy
